{{Short description|Object from algebraic number theory}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''biquadratic field''' is a [[number field]] <math>K</math> of a particular kind, which is a [[Galois extension]] of degree 4 of the [[rational number field]] <math>\Q</math> with [[Galois group]] isomorphic to the [[Klein four-group]].

==Structure and subfields==
Biquadratic fields are obtained by adjoining two [[square root]]s of rational numbers <math>a,b</math>:

: <math> K = \mathbb{Q} \left( \sqrt{a}, \sqrt{b} \right). </math>

Without [[loss of generality]], we may assume ''a'' and ''b'' are non-zero [[square-free integer]]s.

The [[Galois theory|Galois group]] has three [[subgroup]]s of index 2, corresponding to the three [[quadratic field|quadratic subfield]]s  <blockquote><math> \Q(\sqrt a),\Q(\sqrt b),\Q(\sqrt{ab}) \subset K </math>. </blockquote>Biquadratic fields are the simplest examples of [[abelian extension]]s of <math>\Q</math> that are not [[cyclic extension]]s. Also biquadratic fields are usually not [[Monogenic field|monogenic]]: although there exists a [[Primitive element theorem|primitive element]] which generates the field <math>K</math> over <math>\Q</math>, its [[Algebraic integer|ring of integers]] <math>\mathcal{O}_K</math> might not possess a single generator over <math>\Z</math>.
